causal_chain: A counterfactual ablation penalty forces the model to keep ranking margins stable when those selected supports are removed.
A support-selector can learn which historical edges actually justify each positive pair instead of treating all neighbors equally.
Sparse user histories make many positive items explainable by only a small subset of past interactions.
This should suppress brittle popularity/co-occurrence shortcuts and improve full-sort NDCG@10 on held-out items.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: The gain comes from generic extra capacity, residual smoothing, or popularity debiasing rather than from learning a support-sensitive, counterfactually stable explanation of each positive interaction.
discriminative_predictions: A pure residual/dual-path control without counterfactual support-ablation training should underperform the proposed model even when parameter count is matched.
If the mechanism is real, removing the learned support mask at test time should hurt ranking much more than removing a same-sized residual branch.
Improvements should concentrate on sparse users, multi-interest users, and long-tail positives rather than being uniform across all users.
expected_evidence: A larger margin gap between the proposed model and the matched control when support-disagreement is high.
Better NDCG@10 on sparse-user and long-tail slices than on dense-user slices relative to control.
Lower loss sensitivity under leave-one-support-out ablations for held-out positives.
blind_projection.falsifier: If the matched control with the same backbone and parameter budget matches or beats the proposal on full-sort NDCG@10, and the proposal shows no ablation-stability advantage on support-removed positives, the mechanism is not supported.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: The accepted gap was that prior frontier/known-good packages were resource-deferred without mechanism-effect updates, and earlier fresh realizations lacked an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off. Closing that gap requires a custom support-selection plus counterfactual stability objective, not just a configuration tweak of an existing profile.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A pairwise recommender that learns per-positive support selection and trains margins to remain stable under support ablation will rank better than a standard LightGCN/BPR-style control because it captures which historical evidence truly supports each positive while rejecting brittle shortcut co-occurrence.
implementation_requirements: PyTorch implementation of a LightGCN-style encoder
counterfactual leave-one-support-out scoring pass during training
pairwise BPR-compatible objective with stability regularizer
user-specific support-mask module over historical interactions
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Same backbone, same train-only protocol, same split, same evaluation, and matched parameter budget, but with the support-mask and counterfactual stability term disabled.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Add a learned support selector and a counterfactual support-ablation stability objective on top of a LightGCN-style pairwise CF backbone.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: A matched LightGCN/BPR model with dual-path or residual scoring only, but no learned support selection and no ablation-stability regularizer.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: Train the proposed model and a matched dual-path control; compare full-sort NDCG@10 plus leave-one-support-out margin stability on the same frozen ML-1M split.
blind_projection.research_question: Can a pairwise collaborative filter improve full-sort NDCG@10 by learning which historical interactions support each positive target and by enforcing ranking stability when those supports are counterfactually removed?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: The added support-mask and ablation pass should fit within the frozen budget on ML-1M because the extra computation is local to positive-pair training batches and uses the same catalog-wide scoring pipeline as the control.
